quizzes.stem: Scenario: Dmitri's company wants developers limited to two approved models. The platform team sets `model` to the first of them in the managed file and tells the developers to use only those two. What happens when a developer picks another model?

options.a: It is allowed, since only a list restricts a choice
options.b: The choice is refused, because the managed file outranks the developer's own picks
options.c: The pick is refused for the session and restored after the next restart
options.d: The pick stands only if the project file also names that model

explanation.a: A managed `model` is a default, and the lock is the list.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A managed `model` is a **default**: a developer can still pick another model".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a default is overridden at once", so no refusal appears that a restart could lift.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a managed list applies as it is: a project file's list cannot widen it", and nothing here makes a project file's model decide.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Amara adds `allowManagedHooksOnly: true` to the shared project file that her team commits, expecting every developer to be limited to the hooks of the organisation. What is the effect?

options.a: Hooks from the project run, since the team's file is read after the user file
options.b: Every hook is switched off in the project until the managed file confirms it
options.c: Nothing happens, since only the top tier reads that key
options.d: Only the hooks of the project run, since the team's choice is the closest

explanation.c: A lower file that sets a managed-only key has no effect.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A lower file that sets one of these has **no effect**".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page describes "a lock written in the shared project file looks like policy and does nothing", not a switch that waits for confirmation.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Some keys are read only from managed settings, because their purpose is to be out of a developer's reach".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Yusuf's organisation limit is 20000 a month and he has three groups. He proposes limits of 7000, 8000 and 6000 for them. What does the page say about that proposal?

options.a: It is sound, because the organisation limit stops any overspend by the groups
options.b: It breaks the arithmetic, since the parts could together exceed the whole
options.c: It is sound, because unused budget of one group is lent to the others
options.d: It is inconsistent, since each group must have the same limit as the others

explanation.b: Seven thousand, eight thousand and six thousand add up to 21000, which is more than 20000.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "so the organisation limit would decide before the group limits did and nobody would know which one they were under".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page requires that "The group limits add up to the organisation limit and no more", and says nothing about lending.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page's own example has "three groups with 6000, 8000 and 6000 against an organisation limit of 20000", so equal limits are not required.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A platform team wants to show leadership that Claude Code is working. It sets a target of more accepted lines per developer each month and starts the rollout on Monday. What is the main weakness of the plan?

options.a: Accepted lines are not shown on the dashboard and cannot be tracked
options.b: Developers accept fewer lines as they learn, so the figure falls over time
options.c: A monthly target is too coarse to reflect how developers actually work
options.d: Activity rises without any gain, so the figure proves nothing

explanation.a: Ruled out because "The dashboard counts lines accepted as a usage metric".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page's objection is "A target on an activity invites the activity", not the length of the period.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page gives no such trend and rests on the point that "lines accepted can be raised by accepting more lines".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A developer reports that the managed policy "does nothing" for the allowlist of MCP servers on their laptop. The organisation's allowlist, and the key that makes it the only list, are both in the shared project file of the repository. Which fact explains it?

options.a: Lists in settings files merge, so their own list has been added to the policy
options.b: The command line always outranks the managed file, so the list is overridden
options.c: Settings of that kind are honoured at the top tier alone and inert below it
options.d: The shared project file is read first, so the policy file replaced it

explanation.c: A key that only managed settings read has no effect elsewhere.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page orders the levels "highest first" with managed settings above the command line, and "no user, project or local value overrides it".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says managed-only keys are not merged: "A lower file that sets one of these has **no effect**".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Some keys are read only from managed settings, because their purpose is to be out of a developer's reach".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A security lead asks for a way to refuse the options that bring in a plugin, an agent or an MCP server for one run only. Which key does that, and where is it set?

explanation.b: That key rejects the flags that sideload plugins, agents and MCP servers.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "An empty list blocks every source, the official one included", and the allowlist does not stop sideloading.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "only managed hooks run" is what that key does.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The **lock** is `availableModels`, a list" and concerns the model choice.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Before starting a rollout, a team records four weeks of the time to merge for pull requests. Why four weeks, and what does the record allow later?

options.a: Because usage credits reset every four weeks and the data must match
options.b: Because the dashboard keeps only four weeks, so older data is lost
options.c: To show leadership how many lines developers write without the tool
options.d: Because a release cycle fits inside it, so any shift is judged against it

explanation.d: A baseline with a release cycle in it lets a later change be measured.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "enough to include a release cycle and a quiet week", not a limit of the dashboard.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Lines and suggestions accepted are reported and not targeted".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A target on an outcome needs a baseline", and usage credits play no part in it.
